name: Sport and Exercise Science
about: The science of sport and health: physiology, biomechanics, nutrition and sport psychology, with labs and a Sports Training Village on campus, then a research project of your own design in the final two years.

name: Integrated Design Engineering
about: For creative engineers: mechanical, electrical and software skills combined to design products, machines and systems, with core engineering in years 1 and 2 and creative design and innovation after that.

name: Modern Languages (with study or work abroad)
about: Reach fluency in two languages, choosing two advanced ones or one with a beginner language, and learn the culture, history and politics of the countries involved, with a year studying or working abroad.

name: Medicine and Surgery
about: Five years to become a doctor: campus teaching with a weekly clinical-skills day from year 1, including real General Practice, then hospital and community placements in one of the UK's large healthcare regions.

name: Physics and Astrophysics
about: Core physics from entropy to mechanics, plus observational astronomy, in a degree that mixes theory, mathematics, computing and experimental work; accredited by the Institute of Physics.

name: Sport, Exercise and Health Sciences
about: How the body responds to exercise and how to raise performance and health: physiology, anatomy, psychology and biochemistry in labs, a first-year Lake District residential, and advanced options such as extreme environments.

name: BVSc Veterinary Science
about: A five-year vet degree on two campuses: the Clifton city campus and the rural Langford campus, with a small animal referral hospital, dairy farm, anatomy and post-mortem facilities and a clinical skills lab. Case-based learning and placements with many species, ending in supervised core rotations.

name: BEng Aerospace Engineering
about: Aerodynamics, structures and materials, dynamics and control, and systems and design, applied to aircraft, spacecraft and space missions. It is RAeS-accredited, with company contact through the Industrial Liaison Office and a third-year research project such as landing a UAV automatically.

name: BA Liberal Arts
about: An arts and humanities degree with one subject in depth, your pathway, and freedom to range across the rest. Bespoke units put current global issues in historical context and look at how data shapes stories, and you finish with an interdisciplinary project and a capstone on the public role of the humanities.

name: Natural Sciences
about: One broad science degree across 14 departments. You choose three sciences plus a maths course in year one, stay flexible through year two, then specialise in year three, or keep both biological and physical strands. An optional fourth year gives an MSci.

name: Classics
about: Ancient Greece and Rome through their languages, literature, philosophy, history, art and archaeology, working from original texts and objects. With Latin you take three years; with little or no Latin or Greek there is a four-year route that teaches the languages.

name: Economics
about: Core, pure and applied economics in depth, drawing on mathematics, statistics, history, sociology and politics. Past members of the Faculty include Alfred Marshall and John Maynard Keynes, and its staff advise bodies such as the Bank of England and the World Bank.

name: Medicine MBBS
about: A five-year clinically focused degree on the Tooting campus, taught with students of other healthcare professions, with practicals in pathology labs and an anatomy suite, and placements from GP to psychiatry and radiology.

name: Journalism
about: Multimedia journalism with a real-world emphasis: small workshops in reporting and writing, shorthand and photography, electives in English, Sociology, Politics or Creative Writing, and professional work experience.

name: Optometry
about: Four years to train as a registered optometrist: optics, biology, eye disease and lenses, with clinical practice in the University's own eye clinic, City Sight, and 44 weeks of clinical placements, including one at Moorfields.

name: Natural Sciences
about: A flexible science degree for interests that span several subjects, including at least one science. You combine Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Maths, Computer Science and more, with optional Anthropology, Business, Geography or Philosophy. A year abroad or placement can extend it to four years.

name: Archaeology
about: World archaeology from earliest prehistory to the modern day, with training in social and scientific methods. Excavation, fieldwork, osteology, 3D modelling and museum and heritage skills are covered, and you can follow a route accredited by the Chartered Institute for Archaeologists.

name: Law
about: A research-led LLB in the law of England and Wales that forms the first stage of training as a solicitor or barrister. Optional modules let you specialise in public or private law, including international law, and there is a moot court and a pro bono room.

name: Computer Science
about: How computing systems are designed, built and used, from the maths and logic of what can be computed to programming real problems. No programming is assumed; years 1 and 2 leave room for other subjects before you specialise.

name: Veterinary Medicine (5-year programme)
about: Five years to become a vet at the Royal (Dick) School of Veterinary Studies on the Easter Bush campus: how the animal body works in years 1 and 2, then species, disease and treatment, ending in clinical rotations in its own hospitals.

name: Philosophy
about: An undergraduate MA in thinking clearly about the great questions, from mind, language and science to ethics and politics, with more than 40 option courses in years 3 and 4. Philosophy has been taught here since 1583.

name: Veterinary Medicine & Surgery
about: Five years to qualify as a vet on the Garscube campus: body systems and disease in years 1 and 2, then clinical training, ending in a final year with no lectures, working in the school's own practices and hospitals.

name: Computing Science
about: Programming and software engineering first (Python in year 1, Java in year 2), plus algorithms, networks, AI and human-computer interaction, with other subjects in years 1 and 2 and team and individual projects at honours.

name: Marine & Freshwater Biology
about: The study of aquatic environments, with field courses on Loch Lomond and at Millport in the Firth of Clyde, an optional tropical marine field course in the Red Sea, and a research project in the lab or in the field.

name: Aeronautical Engineering
about: An integrated master's on how vehicles and structures interact with air: aerodynamics, structures, flight mechanics, propulsion and control. Year two includes a flight-testing course at Cranfield; a year abroad or a year in industry can be added.

name: Medicine
about: A six-year integrated course that ends in both an MBBS and a BSc. You meet patients and clinical skills early, do research in phase two, and can follow specialist pathways such as neuroscience or mental health. Teaching is across north and west London campuses and NHS partners.

name: Chemistry
about: Core and applied chemistry to master's level: inorganic, organic, physical, analytical, synthetic and computational, with an extensive laboratory programme. It ends in a six-month research project in an academic group; year-in-industry and year-abroad versions exist.

name: War Studies
about: War, conflict and security studied through history, politics, international relations, philosophy and sociology. Year one gives the causes and consequences of war; later years add specialist options, a Cold War module and a dissertation. One language module is free, and a year abroad is optional.

name: Law LLB
about: Law studied as an intellectual discipline at the Dickson Poon School of Law in Somerset House, near the Royal Courts of Justice and Inns of Court. It has a professional skills portfolio with a legal clinic and mooting, and dual-degree and study-abroad options after year one.

name: Neuroscience
about: The nervous system from cells and development to physiology and pharmacology, linked to psychology and philosophy. It stresses developmental neuroscience, disorders of the nervous system and clinical aspects, with a substantial research project and optional placement or year abroad.

name: Medicine and Surgery
about: Learn the body's systems together, meet simulated patients in year 1, then train on placements across Lancashire, Cumbria and Yorkshire with more than 70 healthcare providers, with a chance to intercalate between years 4 and 5.

name: Environmental Science
about: Weather, climate, hydrology and flood risk in year 1, biogeochemistry, ecology and soil science in year 2, and a dissertation in year 3 by fieldwork, lab work or modelling, with field trips in the Lake District and Yorkshire Dales.

name: Linguistics
about: How language works and is used: phonetics, phonology, grammar and pragmatics, and language in politics, health, business and law, with access to phonetics, eye-tracking, perception and EEG labs.

name: Medicine and Surgery
about: A five-year route to becoming a doctor, with clinical placements from year one, teaching by practising clinicians, and a course built to prepare you for clinical practice as a holistic doctor.

name: Environmental Science
about: The biosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and geosphere and how society interacts with them, with fieldwork in every year, training in data and coding, and an independent research project in your final year.

name: Ancient History
about: The civilisations of ancient Greece, Rome and Persia: their politics, culture and society, the lives of ordinary people as well as great figures, and how to weigh the evidence, with archaeology and literary analysis.

name: Sport and Exercise Science
about: Physiology, biochemistry, biomechanics, motor control and psychology behind human performance, in specialist labs on a campus with elite athlete programmes, plus a research project and an optional placement year.

name: Industrial Design
about: Design products for people: research, ideation, model making and CAD in year 1, design for manufacture in year 2, then a year-long self-directed project, with an optional paid placement year in industry.

name: Aeronautical Engineering
about: Sustainable propulsion, autonomous flight, aircraft systems and computational fluid dynamics, with a flight test module of up to four flights in a flying laboratory and a final-year aircraft design project.

name: Economics
about: Economic theory and practice applied to questions such as inequality, pay gaps and climate change. A core in microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometrics, then specialist economics courses and outside options from other departments; a year abroad is open by application.

name: International Relations
about: Why states go to war, cooperate or obey international law, and how institutions such as the UN and EU work. It covers the history, theory and politics of the international system, with an option to add a language specialism to your degree certificate.

name: LLB Bachelor of Laws
about: Law studied from a social science perspective, covering the knowledge needed for the first stage of the Solicitors Qualifying Exam and qualifying as a law degree for the Bar. Mooting competitions and events with the Inns of Court sit alongside the course.

name: Computer Science
about: A broad, flexible computer science degree: you choose units to follow your interests and specialise in years 2 and 3, with a team project in year 1 and an optional year in industry on a sister course.

name: Materials Science and Engineering
about: How the properties of metals, polymers, ceramics and nanomaterials such as graphene come from their structure, and how to engineer them. Taught in the Home of Engineering and Materials building, beside the National Graphene Institute.

name: Medicine
about: A five-year route to becoming a doctor, learned through themed case discussions, anatomy dissection and clinical placements across Greater Manchester from the first years, with a student-chosen Personal Excellence Path.

name: Medicine BMBS
about: Five years to become a doctor, with clinical experience built in throughout, placements with NHS trusts across the East Midlands, and competence milestones tracked as you go towards working as a foundation doctor.

name: Veterinary Medicine and Surgery
about: A five-year vet degree with hands-on animal handling from day one in a purpose-built school, small animal, farm and equine practice, and a third-year research project that adds the BVMedSci. Two intakes: September and April.

name: History
about: History from the early medieval era to today across the Americas, Europe, Africa and Asia, taught through curiosity, critique and curation, with access to the University's manuscripts and special collections.

name: Philosophy, Politics and Economics (PPE)
about: Three subjects in one degree: philosophy for clear argument, politics for how institutions shape societies, economics for how choices allocate resources. After year one you can keep all three or drop to two, and choose options such as sociology or international relations.

name: Computer Science
about: Computer systems understood through mathematical reasoning: you prove how programs and networks behave, not only build them. Core topics fill year one and part of year two, then options; in year two a group design practical may be sponsored by industry.

name: English Language and Literature
about: Writing in English from Anglo-Saxon England to today, including work from outside Britain and in translation. One-to-one tutorials, a Shakespeare portfolio, an 8,000-word dissertation and a special option chosen from around 25.

name: Medicine (5 Year Programme)
about: Five years to become a doctor, seeing patients from your first week in community and hospital settings, with modules you choose yourself, from the fundamental and clinical sciences to psychological and social ones.

name: Applied Artificial Intelligence
about: Practical AI projects set by researchers and industry from year 1, teaching from academics involved in the ATLAS experiment at CERN, and a 60-credit Applied AI in Industry project in your final year.

name: Theatre and Performance
about: Theatre and performance studied in practice and in theory, working with the BLOC Arts Centre and partners such as the V&A, the Barbican, the Live Art Development Agency and Shakespeare's Globe, with an optional year abroad.

name: International Relations
about: The origins of war and peace, foreign policy, trade, terrorism, human rights and international law. You take two other subjects alongside it in year one, then specialise in years three and four, ending in a 12,000-word dissertation. The MA here is the equivalent of a BA.

name: Astrophysics
about: The Universe from extrasolar planets and black holes to galaxy clusters, about half core physics and maths and half astrophysics. You model systems and analyse large data sets, can use telescopes at the University Observatory, and finish with a major project.

name: Medicine BSc (Hons) A100
about: A six-year route: three years in St Andrews building science and clinical skills for a BSc, then three years at a partner medical school for an MBChB or MBBS. Students classed as overseas for fees complete their training at the University of Manchester.

name: Fine Art
about: At Chelsea College of Arts: an experimental course built around exhibitions, projects, publications and performances, where you develop your own independent art practice and set it in a wider social context.

name: Graphic Communication Design
about: At Central Saint Martins: creative, conceptual, technical and critical skills for 21st-century designers, across a range of graphic communication practices that cross traditional boundaries, used to tackle environmental and social questions.

name: Fashion Design Technology: Womenswear
about: At London College of Fashion: an in-depth study of womenswear design, technology and production, with brand links and a short industry placement, plus sustainable production and inclusive design.

name: Arts and Sciences (Societies) BASc
about: An interdisciplinary degree taught only at UCL. A shared Core teaches you to work across arts, social science and science, then you choose specialist modules from across the university, study a modern language throughout and can take internships. Societies is one of three pathways.

name: Architecture BSc
about: Architecture learned in a studio: drawing, model-making and portfolio work from day one. From year two you join a Bartlett Design Unit, a small studio led by practising architects, with themes from craft and film to philosophy and science, plus a first-year international field trip.

name: Economics BSc (Econ)
about: Economic theory with the maths and statistics to use it, applied to questions such as climate change, inequality and inflation. Students can present research at the annual Explore Econ conference and hear visiting economists at the Stone Centre and finance lectures.

name: Economics
about: Micro, macro and econometrics taught through research, from abstract models to empirical tests of markets, institutions and public policy. A flexible structure lets you take options inside or outside the department, including Business School, Politics, Philosophy and Computer Science modules.

name: Computer Science
about: An accredited degree built on principles rather than fashions: software engineering, algorithm analysis and system design, taught from first principles with no programming assumed. You complete an individual project in year three and can add a year in industry, research or abroad.

name: Ancient History and Classical Archaeology
about: The history, art and archaeology of the ancient Mediterranean through texts, images and material remains. You handle real artefacts, can join fieldwork in Greece, visit sites and museums, and take part in an annual classical play staged at a professional theatre. An ancient language is optional.

name: International Studies in Education
about: Education in a global and multicultural frame, taught wholly in English: sociology of education, child development, globalisation and migration, with a language-teaching or international-education route.

name: English Studies
about: English linguistics and literature, English-speaking cultures and English as an international language, for students already fluent; the first year can be taken entirely by distance learning.

name: Contemporary Dance Practices BA
about: Three-year contemporary dance degree taught in English: daily technical training, improvisation and composition, theory, and a fifth semester on exchange or in a professional internship. 180 ECTS.

name: Bachelor in Physiotherapy
about: Anatomy, physiology, pathology and kinesiology with physiotherapeutic assessment and treatment methods, taught in English. It is the first stage: the licence to practise needs the master's.

name: Bachelor in Osteopathy
about: Assessment, diagnosis and treatment of musculoskeletal dysfunction from a holistic view, mixing theory and practical courses in English. 180 ECTS, accredited by Luxembourg's ministry.

name: Bachelor in Sport and Exercise Science
credential: Bachelor in Sport and Exercise Science
about: How body and mind respond to training and physical activity, and what shapes health and performance, with block teaching in English; leads to coaching, teaching or research.

name: Bachelor in International Sport Management
about: Business knowledge and management skills for the international sport industry, taught in English in blocks, with internships, student projects and a network of sport organisations.

name: Bachelor in Nutrition, Fitness and Health
credential: Bachelor in Nutrition, Fitness and Health
about: Nutrition science, health promotion and disease prevention across the lifecycle and in exercise, taught in English in small groups, combining theory with applied learning.

name: Bachelor in Computer Science
about: Programming, theory and mathematics built on international ACM/IEEE curriculum standards, with practice through research and development projects. English-led, with a little French or German; leads on to a master's.

name: Bachelor en Enseignement musical (Bachelor in Music Education)
about: A teacher-training and artistic degree for advanced musicians, taught in English: you specialise in instrument or voice, solfège, or early-childhood music education.

name: Electrical Engineering
about: A 120-credit Fulton Schools of Engineering degree on circuits, signals, control, electromagnetics, power and quantum engineering, with hands-on problem-solving as Arizona's semiconductor industry grows.

name: Economics
about: Economics treats markets, firms, legislatures and families as systems of people pursuing goals through institutions, tested with data, models and mathematical and statistical tools.

name: Computer Science
about: Taught through Harvard College and the School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, with a concurrent AB/SM master's option for qualified undergraduates. CS 50 has no prerequisites.

name: Computer Science
about: The BS in Computer Science from the Grainger College of Engineering, taught through the Siebel School of Computing and Data Science, with a rigorous computer science and technical core and 17+ blended CS degrees.

name: Accountancy
about: A Gies College of Business major on how money and other assets flow through businesses and economies; you can explore before you declare, and Gies also offers an Accountancy + Data Science option.

name: Bachelor of Business Administration
about: The four-year Michigan Ross business degree, with classes at Ross from first year and action-based learning in which students start, advise, invest in and lead real businesses.

name: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
about: Course 6 runs a family of degrees from electrical science to computer science, AI and decision-making, computation and cognition, and computer science with economics and data science, with a hands-on approach.

name: Business and Political Economy
about: A Stern degree that combines business and political economy coursework with two required semesters of study away: sophomore fall in London and junior spring in Shanghai.

name: Computer Science
about: A broad, rigorous training in the science of computing: a 96-unit major with a core, then a track such as artificial intelligence, systems, theory or human-computer interaction. No prior coding is assumed.

name: Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences
about: First-years are admitted directly into the EECS major and stay four years, with a hands-on, interdisciplinary curriculum in electrical engineering and computer science.

name: Spieker Undergraduate Business Program (Haas)
about: The Berkeley Haas four-year BS in Business Administration. High school seniors apply on the UC application, then submit a Haas supplement with an essay and a video interview upload.

name: Global Affairs
about: A major at the Jackson School of Global Affairs built on multidisciplinary core courses linking recurring political, economic and social issues across countries and time, taught in small cohorts.

name: Computer Science
about: Yale Engineering's department teaches the strengths and limits of computation and how to invent new computing systems; Yale also lists joint majors with economics, mathematics, psychology and linguistics.
